subject: Key return process and operator telemetry visibility for private deployment
messages:
From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@aureliahealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com, legal@aureliahealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Key-return expectations for private on-prem deployment

Irene,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As we move toward contract, Legal and Security have two pockets of questions that we need to document in the DPA appendix for our private deployment (air-gapped on-prem variant + VPC-admin plane):

1) Key return / key destruction: If Aurelia terminates the contract or requests migration, what exactly is the step-by-step process for returning customer-managed keys (CMKs) or performing a verified destruction? Is there an escrow option?

2) Operator visibility: your sales deck mentioned that Redwood operators do not have plaintext key access, but Security wants to know what telemetry and system-level logs the operator team can see during a recover/restore or emergency break-glass event. What fields are recorded and how long are those logs retained?

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfer: Please confirm which subprocessors would be involved in any recovery operations and whether that could trigger cross-border transfers that we need to flag in our GDPR appendix.

Attaching the redline Legal asked us to start with. Can you confirm the DPA edits needed and whether these items map to a standard addendum or require bespoke language?

Appreciate a short written reply we can attach to the redline.

Best,
Sam
CISO, Aurelia Health

Attachment: aurelia_dpa_redline_v1.pdf

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key-return expectations for private on-prem deployment

Hi Sam — thanks for the concrete list. High-level answers below; I’m attaching our recommended exit flow and the current subprocessor register so Legal can see names/locations. Karthik will follow up with the operator/telemetry specifics.

1) Key return / destruction options:
- Customer-managed KMS (recommended): We deploy the Private Control Plane with an integration to your KMS; you retain keys and we never ingest plaintext key material. At termination you keep keys; no return needed.
- Customer key-in-Redwood (custody): If you choose Redwood-managed keys, we offer two termination paths: (a) export and encrypted handoff of key blobs to an escrow target you control (PGP/GPG or HSM bundle), or (b) verified destruction with an attestation report. Escrow requires a mutually-agreed export format and transfer method (SFTP or physical HSM courier).
- Escrow/transfer windows and additional fees are in the addendum; current standard is 30 days to complete export unless otherwise negotiated.

2) Operator visibility and telemetry (summary):
- Operators do not have access to plaintext CEKs when you use customer-managed KMS.
- During emergency support (break-glass) we can perform a constrained restore using encrypted artifacts only; operator actions are gated by approval workflow and are auditable.
- Logged fields: operation id, operator id, command invoked, timestamps, artifact checksum, source/destination hostnames, and encrypted artifact reference. No plaintext data or keys are logged.
- Retention: default 90 days; options for 365 days available as an enterprise setting.

3) Subprocessors & transfers:
- The attached CSV shows subprocessors involved in support, telemetry ingestion, and courier services. Most subprocessors are US-based; a small set (monitoring provider) is EU-based and only handles encrypted metadata.
- Restoration or couriering of escrowed key material may require cross-border transfer depending on escrow target. We will document any transfer and execute SCCs or addendum language as required.

Next steps: Karthik to provide a technical appendix for the DPA that we can attach; Marissa will pick up procurement timing and the DocuSign/HubSpot artifacts.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: keystore_exit_flow_v2.pptx, subprocessors_current_20261020.csv

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@aureliahealth.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key-return expectations for private on-prem deployment

Sam — quick technical appendix you can paste into the DPA. Happy to expand if you want explicit clauses.

Operator telemetry and breakpoint procedures (detailed):
- Break-glass flow: Customer raises incident via the private control plane (or calls the emergency number). Two-person approval from customer security + designated Redwood on-call required to initiate recovery. All actions require an immutable ticket recorded in the control plane.
- Encrypted artifacts only: Operators manipulate encrypted model checkpoints and metadata. Key material (KEKs/CEKs) is never exposed in process memory or logs. When an operator triggers a transfer/export, the system streams an encrypted blob to the configured escrow endpoint; operator sees only status codes and blob checksums.
- Least-privilege operator roles: separation between support (diagnostics) and recovery (export). Recovery role requires key custodial approvals attested in the ticket.
- Audit evidence provided: SHA256 checksums of exported blobs, transfer logs (SFTP session ids / courier manifest numbers), timestamped operator IDs, and the signed attestation of destruction if chosen.
- Subprocessor involvement: If a subcontractor (e.g., monitoring vendor) helps with diagnostics, they only receive encrypted metadata and anonymized telemetry. They cannot initiate exports.

I can convert the above into a short DPA clause and we can drop it into the redline under "Operator Access and Key Escrow". Let me know if Aurelia needs HSM-to-HSM transfer language or a KMS-specific format (AWS/GCP/PKCS#11).

— Karthik
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@aureliahealth.com>

Cc: legal@aureliahealth.com, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2026 16:48:00 -07:00

Irene / Karthik — this is perfect, thanks. Legal will take your suggested clause and adapt the redline. A few quick follow-ups so we close out our checklist before procurement: 

• Please add explicit language that operators cannot request an export without the customer ticket and two-person approval.
• Can you confirm the retention SLA for the transfer logs (we prefer 1 year, but can accept 90 days if there’s a contract exception)?
• For escrow: we prefer HSM-to-HSM transfer where possible. If Redwood supports PKCS#11 bundle export, flag that in the DPA.

If you can attach the suggested DPA paragraph and update the redline to reflect the approval gating, we’ll route to Legal this afternoon.

Thanks — Sam
CISO, Aurelia Health
